title: Shortest String That Contains Three Strings
statement: You get three strings `a`, `b` and `c`. Build the shortest possible string in which each of the three appears as a substring (a contiguous run of characters). When several strings of that minimal length work, return the one that comes first alphabetically: compare two equal-length strings at the first index where they differ, and the one with the earlier letter there is smaller.
constraints: a, b and c contain only lowercase English letters
signature: String minimumString(String a, String b, String c)
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every candidate string by length is hopeless beyond tiny inputs. Instead, notice that in an optimal answer the three strings appear in some left-to-right order, and each one should overlap its left neighbour as much as possible. There are only 3! = 6 orders, so enumerate them all, glue the strings greedily in each order, and keep the best result.

Gluing `second` onto `first` has two cases: if `second` already sits inside `first`, nothing is added; otherwise find the longest suffix of `first` that equals a prefix of `second` and append only the rest of `second`.

## Approach

1. `merge(first, second)` returns `first` when it already contains `second`.
2. Otherwise try overlaps `k` from the longest possible down to 1; the first `k` where `first` ends with the first `k` letters of `second` wins, and we append `second.slice(k)`.
3. With no overlap at all, simply concatenate.
4. For each of the 6 orders `[x, y, z]`, build `merge(merge(x, y), z)`.
5. Keep the shortest `candidate`, breaking length ties by the alphabetically smaller string.

## Example 1, step by step

`a = "abc"`, `b = "bca"`, `c = "aaa"`. Order `(a, b, c)`: `"abc"` and `"bca"` overlap on `"bc"`, giving `"abca"`; then `"aaa"` overlaps on `"a"`, giving `"abcaaa"` (length 6). Order `(c, a, b)`: `"aaa"` + `"abc"` overlap on `"a"` gives `"aaabc"`; adding `"bca"` overlaps on `"bc"`, giving `"aaabca"` (length 6). No order is shorter than 6, and `"aaabca"` is the smallest of the length-6 results, so it is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L²) with L ≤ 300: six orders, each trying up to L overlaps that compare up to L characters.
- Space: O(L) for the candidate strings.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the containment check: `merge("abc", "b")` must stay `"abc"`, not become `"abcb"`.
- Trying overlaps from short to long gives a longer result; start from the longest.
- Several orders can give the same length; break the tie by comparing the strings themselves, not by keeping whichever order came first.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `merge` | glues two strings with the largest possible overlap |
| `k` | the overlap length being tried |
| `orders` | the six orderings of `a`, `b`, `c` |
| `candidate` | merged string for the current order |
| `best` | shortest, then smallest, candidate so far |

narration.2: merge glues second onto the end of first with as much overlap as possible.
narration.3: If second is already inside first, gluing adds nothing.
narration.4: Try overlap lengths from the longest possible down to 1.
narration.5: Does first end with the first k letters of second?
narration.6: Yes: append only the part of second that is not shared.
narration.9: No overlap at all, so the strings are simply joined.
narration.12: List all six orders in which the three strings can appear.
narration.14: Enumerate the orders one by one.
narration.15: Glue the three strings together in this order.
narration.16: A strictly shorter candidate always wins.
narration.18: Among equally short candidates, keep the alphabetically smaller one.
narration.22: best is the shortest, alphabetically first string that contains all three.
